_description: Battle simulator v1 (tools/nn/sim, docs/en/training/simulator.md): the numbers that are neither in a unit passport (config/nn/units.json) nor in the game's rules (config/nn/game_rules.json). Each is measured in the game or calibrated to a measurement (docs/en/training/measurements.md); `why` says which. Written by hand; python -m tools.nn.sim.check compares the simulator with the game.

step_s.why: morale rises 2 points a second before contact in every recording (+0.057 MoralePercent/s at leadership 35 ... +0.029 at 70) = one point (minimium_increment_update_per_tick) per 0.5 s tick

battle_limit_s.why: network plan: 60 minutes, the attacker loses on time

map_half_m.why: measured: routing units leave the map at |x| or |z| = 1020 m (Crossroads flat, 28 runs)

melee_depth.why: ranks (c; 0: off; geometry.dims, the companion's exchange.gaps the same): a formation in melee (its melee clock contact_s > 0; the companion: the game's melee flag) does not close up as its men fall: ranks = max(ceil(r), min(r + c (1 - men / men0), ceil(men0 / files0))), r = men / files, files0 = floor(width / h) - the dead leave c ranks' worth of room at their whole loss; out of melee the box closes up as before (the missile probe P1: a target thinned by fire re-forms). MEASURED from the soldiers' places once a second, not a rule of the game (no rule for the shape of a thinned formation in CA's material, the database or the community's write-ups): the probes reform, reform2, damaged (build/charge-probe/runs/20261008-180435, -181311, -175102, -175151; one on one, 240 s from 3 m; not the enveloping 15 / 50 m clanrats nor the two-on-one lane), 72 lane-sides, 4,314 melee seconds from 5 s after contact (build/formdepth/shape.py, fit.py, fit3.py): the depth of the men along the facing (p3-p97 / 0.94) as ranks against the same unit whole before contact - at 90-100 / 50-60 / 30-40 / 10-20 / 0-10 % of the men the game holds 6.5 / 5.2 / 4.4 / 3.5 / 3.4 ranks (lane medians) where the closed-up box has 6.0 / 4.0 / 4.0 / 2.0 / 1.0 and the rule 6.0 / 4.6 / 4.9 / 3.8 / 3.1; the width stays near the ordered (swordsmen at 50 % 28.5 of 29.3 m, the files kept as dims). c fitted 2.8 [0.4-4.3, 90 % lane bootstrap] (the front half alone, centroid to the front men: 2.6); r + c (1 - share) fits better than a power of the share (a 0.53), a floor of ranks or ceil(r) + c (lane-weighted squared error 8.31 against 8.41 / 8.31 / 8.75; the closed-up box 8.75). Contact at the game's places on the same probes (build/formdepth/probe_contact.py, both in melee, >= 5 s after contact, contact.engage on): the sim touches in 91.2 -> 98.0 % of the seconds (the weaker unit at 50-70 / 30-50 / < 30 % of its men 87.6 / 88.5 / 87.2 -> 96.4 / 99.2 / 100 %); the box gap stays at the whole units' level best at c ~2.2 (at 2.8 the < 30 % bin overlaps 1.2 m more than whole units). OFF: no whole-battle lever. With 2.8, step replay of the 92 battles (exam 20 / 72; build/formdepth/sr_pos_md28, sr_free_md28 against build/contactgap/sr_pos_rect, sr_free_rect): --force pos melee windows with no sim contact 17.6 / 13.6 % -> 14.9 / 12.4 %, HP lost a window 0.96 / 0.92 -> 0.98 / 0.93, routs begun 1.34 / 1.22 -> 1.39 / 1.25, but units under 30 % health in melee 1.08 / 1.03 -> 1.21 / 1.10 (the sim already over-hits thinned targets; more contact makes it worse - a thinned target's men within the strikers' reach are not modelled); free: HP 1.02 / 0.96 -> 1.04 / 0.97, routs 1.38 / 1.25 -> 1.40 / 1.28; the 72 whole battles (build/formdepth/r72_md28.json): routs a unit 0.832 -> 0.847 (game 1.187), same winner 59.5 -> 58.5 of 72, enemy HP lost 0.501 -> 0.497 (0.571).

formation.why: spacing_m: a man's place across the front and between ranks for a unit WITHOUT a formation template (every unit of ours has one: config/nn/units.json spacing, the database's unit_spacings close formation of land_units.spacing - Empire infantry and lords 1.48 x 1.6 m, clanrats / clanrat spearmen / flagellants / militia 1.6 x 1.7, greatswords 1.7 x 1.75, stormvermin 1.8 x 1.9, skavenslaves 1.6 x 1.8, slingers / night runners 2.2 x 2.8, archers 2.0 x 2.1). files = floor(ordered width / h), front files x h, depth ceil(men / files) x v: the game's own formations (data/roster, 6 units, 15-80 m) give front (files - 1) h within 1.3 % (median), depth (ranks - 1) v within 14 % (wide fronts deeper: scatter); build/meleecore/spacing_check.py. Before 06.10.2026: 1.5 m for every unit (an arena spearmen fit). build/mass/spec.md read the template's numbers one row off (1.65 x 1.75 for the Empire: the next row's): the table's rows put nine floats BEFORE the key; that layout reads all 164 rows to the last byte (tools/nn/dbtables.py unit_spacings) and fits the roster depths (1.65 x 1.75 gave the Empire's depth x0.77-0.92).

turn.why: formation_deg_s: out of melee a standing formation (not walking) turns in place at most this fast (a shooter turning to its target: measured 04.10.2026, build/p3, 210 arena runs, 1 s samples: missile units p50 81 deg/s, 858 episodes; melee infantry 72; there is no game rule for a formation's turn - the database's turn_rate is a man's). A lone man (a lord) standing turns at his own turn rate: the database's battle_entities turn_rate (General 120, Warlord 180 deg/s; config/nn/units.json speed.turn_deg_s); the fitted single_deg_s 40 is gone. move_turn (1: on): a unit on the move turns towards its point at its men's turn rate (the database) and runs only the way it faces (speed x cos of the angle off, none beyond 90 deg); before, it faced the way it walked at once (an about-face in one 0.5 s step). The turning probe (build/movelords, tools.nn.charge_probe --plan move battle 1, 0.25 s samples, soldier places): spearmen ordered to run to a point 150 m behind them about-faced where they stood (each man's place along the new front against the old: correlation -0.98 - the front rank became the back; the unit's bearing turned 180 deg in ~1 s) and their centre reached the run 2.0 s after the order (0.45 / 1.1 / 2.3 / 3.0 m/s at 0.5 / 1 / 1.5 / 2 s); 120 m to the side: 2.3 m/s at 1.3 s, 3.0 at 2 s; the General turned 180 deg on a move order at ~120 deg/s, the Warlord at ~200 (the database: 120 / 180), both moved off 1.2 s after the order and reached 0.9 of the run at ~3 / 2 s. A facing order in place (the simulator has none): spearmen 90 deg in 5-6 s (men moved ~8 m: the formation re-forms), 180 deg in 4.8 s (an about-face, correlation -0.97); the General 180 / 90 deg in 2.1 / 2.4 s (~110 deg/s after ~0.7 s), the Warlord 3.0 / 2.1 s (~75 deg/s - slower than on a move order and than the database's 180: OPEN). Before 06.10.2026: formation_deg_s / single_deg_s: out of melee a standing unit (not walking) turns in place at most this fast (a lord or another single entity: single_deg_s); a walking unit faces the way it walks, in melee contact.melee_turn_deg_s holds. Measured 04.10.2026 (build/p3, all 210 arena runs with 1 s samples since 30.09): missile units standing out of melee whose engine target becomes an enemy 60 deg or more off their bearing faced it within 20 deg after 1 s (median; mean 1.6 s for 60-120 deg, 1.7 s for 120-180 deg; 97 % of 160 within 15 s), (angle - 20) / seconds p25 45 / p50 64 / p75 117 deg/s - a lower bound, a turn done within the second counts a whole second; turning episodes of standing units (mv off, < 0.3 m/s, out of melee, >= 60 deg): missile infantry p50 81 deg/s (858), melee infantry 72 (23: they rarely stand and turn), lords 40 (p25 31, p75 66; 440 episodes, 2 s for 60-100 deg). 80 for formations, 40 for single entities. Before: the bearing was set at once, so a standing shooter facing away shot at once.

contact.engage_release_why: engage_release ON (1; 0: off; battle.py after the leave rules): the engage hold is for units that stay fighting - a pair where either unit leaves (a withdraw, a far move, an attack_leave, a skirmish run) or has an attack order on another unit touches only by the old hold (reach_m + hold_m; contact_limit engage=False); the chase and the rout's stuck men keep their own contacts. The game: fatleave (build/probes7/leavefat.py) - an unchased leaver is out of the enemy's melee at 5.5-6 s and loses 17-82 HP over 10 s; the sim with the engage hold on the leaver: out at 5 s, 120 HP; released: 4 s, 92 HP (as before engage). The fresh probe (build/charge-probe/runs/20261008-145559, -145641): swordsmen told in melee to attack clanrats beside the ones they fight turned 75-80 deg and walked 8 m, touching them 4.5-5.5 s after the order. 72 gate battles (4 copies, build/engagefix): same winner 58 -> 60.5 of 72, routs a unit 0.803 -> 0.821 (game 1.187), enemy HP lost 0.505 -> 0.501 (0.571), own 0.683 -> 0.682 (0.784). Step replay --force pos (92 battles, exam / 72): melee windows without a contact 17.6 / 13.6 % (unchanged), HP lost a window 0.95 / 0.92 (0.96 / 0.92).
contact.engage_why: engage OFF (0; 1: on; geometry.engage_gap / contact_limit, battle.py, replay.py, stepreplay.py, companion exchange.gaps). On: two formations either of which is in melee already stay in contact while their outer men are within the game's formed combat distance - the boxes' edge gap up to the database's entity_action_attack_formed_combat_distance (2.5 m) + the larger man's radius (battle_entities, 0.55-0.9) - half a man's place of each formation towards the other (sp_v through the front or back, sp_h through a flank: the outer men stand that far inside the box, dims depth = ranks x v); never less than reach_m + hold_m; Empire infantry on clanrats +1.5 m (hold_m: -0.5). The start of a contact (reach_m) and a lone man's rule are unchanged. Database numbers, no fit. The probes with soldier places (reform, reform2, defender: 2499 lane-seconds of 1 v 1 melee after its first 5 s; build/contactgap/probe_shape.py): the two units' closest men stand 0.95-1.75 m apart (10-90 %, median 1.39 - inside the combat distance), the simulator's boxes at the same centres -3.1..+2.3 m (median -0.1): the old hold finds contact in 42 % of those seconds, engage in 81 % (the rest: the game's formation keeps its depth as men fall - swordsmen at 50 of 120 men ~8 m deep - while the box loses ranks, 4.8 m). The 92 recorded battles at the game's places (build/contactgap/rules.py, every second): the game's melee seconds with a contact 65.0 -> 72.5 % (of the HP lost in them 72.7 -> 79.5 %; with rect_gap too 84.8 / 89.5 %), false contacts (no game melee flag within 3 s) 12.5k -> 14.2k unit-s (+0.4 % of 371k melee unit-s; rect_gap too 18.9k). Step replay (10 s windows, exam / 72 battles): pos-forced melee windows without a contact 43.6 / 29.5 % -> 34.4 / 23.0 % (with rect_gap + push_keep_facing 17.6 / 13.6 %), HP lost a window 0.79 / 0.85 -> 0.84 / 0.87 (0.96 / 0.92), the new contacts' damage at the game's (touching 2+ enemies 0.97 / 1.00), rout starts 1.07 / 1.03 -> 1.13 / 1.09 (1.34 / 1.22: the simulator routs more than the game from the same state already); free HP 0.96 / 0.94 -> 0.98 / 0.95 (1.02 / 0.96), routs 1.21 / 1.11 -> 1.25 / 1.15 (1.38 / 1.25). The 72 battles (4 copies): routs a unit 0.802 -> 0.824 (with rect_gap + push_keep_facing 0.832; game 1.187), same winner 57.5 -> 58 (59.5) of 72, enemy HP lost 0.501 -> 0.504 (0.501; 0.571), own 0.668 -> 0.676 (0.677; 0.784). Off until decided (it changes the simulator's version).
contact.rect_gap_why: rect_gap OFF (geometry.rect_gap, battle.py, replay.py; true: on; false / absent: the centre-line gap). On, the gap between two formations' edges - the contact test (reach_m, hold_m), the closing up, the charge's reach - is the true signed distance of their rectangles (the shortest edge-to-edge distance when apart, minus the least depth of the overlap when they overlap: the separating-axis test over the four edge normals), not the distance along the line between the centres less each rectangle's half extent along it. Head-on, centres on one line, the two are the same (reach_m was measured so); at an angle or offset the centre-line gap misses boxes whose corners meet off that line. A lone man (a circle) keeps the centre-line gap. Geometry, no new number. Teacher-forced step replay of the 72 battles (3 s windows from the game's places, build/simreal/stepwin; build/meleegap2/stepgap.py): of the windows where the game's unit is in melee the centre-line test finds no enemy formation in contact in 35 % (enemy) / 27 % (own), where the simulator then loses 0.35-0.73 of the game's health; in 39 % / 42 % of those the rectangles overlap by 0.5 m or more. Exam replay (itS24 / itS24ai, 6 copies): enemy routs a battle 9.70 -> 11.07 (network) / 10.68 -> 10.67 (ai_like), game 16.0 / 16.3; enemy health lost in melee a unit 0.475 -> 0.480 / 0.435 -> 0.440 (game 0.547 / 0.538); the 72 battles: routs a unit 0.812 -> 0.815 (game 1.187), same winner 60 -> 58.5 of 72. Kept off: the walkpass2 probe twin (tools/nn/walkpass_probe.py, 40 lanes) gets worse - a walker clipping held clanrats by 2 / 5 m pushes on at 1.61 / 0.93 m/s at a run (centre-line 2.47 / 1.46, game 2.68 / 2.39), at a walk 0.91 / 0.63 (1.22 / 0.91, game 1.33 / 0.97): the held clanrats turn towards it and their turned box keeps the corner overlap the centre-line test missed. To turn on together with that (the held unit turning in place, or move_push measured with the rectangle gap). The stall's cause (build/adjmelee, the facing traced): not the clanrats' turn (with melee_turn_deg_s 0 the walker was as slow) but the walker's own - slowed in the clanrats' box it turned to them (battle.py, the face to the opponent of a unit under 0.3 m/s) and ran only cos(53 deg) of its speed to its point; contact.push_keep_facing removes it: the walkpass2 clip lanes' mean error of the push 0.335 m/s centre line, 0.531 rect, 0.346 rect with push_keep_facing, square_front and the frontage (16 lane kinds, 4 copies).
contact.square_front_why: square_front OFF (battle.py, the facing in melee; 1: on). Formation against formation the fight's anchor is the unit's attack target where it touches it, else its nearest opponent; a formation attacking its anchor faces square to the anchor's side it touches (the fronts parallel), not the anchor's centre; one not attacking it keeps its facing and turns (square to that side) only to an anchor attacking it from outside contact.front_deg. The sidecontact probe (tools/nn/charge_probe.py --plan sidecontact; build/adjmelee/runs/20261014-111840, -111937: swordsmen attack held clanrats at a walk from 3 m, 0 / 6 / 12 / 18 m off their line, a second clanrat unit 1 m beside the target, 2 lanes a case): the game's swordsmen turned 6-16 deg on the way in and back to 180-186 in melee, sliding to 3.2 / 5.7 / 7.4 m off; the held clanrats stayed at 3-5 deg; the twin turned both to the other's centre (206 / 17 deg) and the attacker's box corner left the bystander (it lost 0-1.5 HP/s from 30 s on against the game's 6.2-9.5). With it (and rect_gap): 2.7 / 5.1 / 7.6 m off. Whole battles (exam replay, 6 copies; rect_gap + push_keep_facing + square_front): enemy routs a battle 9.70 -> 10.27 (network) / 10.68 -> 10.46 (ai_like; game 16.0 / 16.3), enemy melee loss a unit 0.475 -> 0.474 / 0.435 -> 0.433 (game 0.547 / 0.538): no lever on the routs, kept off.
contact.push_keep_facing_why: push_keep_facing OFF (battle.py, the facing in melee; 1: on): a formation under a move to a point farther than step_m does not turn to the enemy it touches (it keeps the facing of its way). The walkpass2 probe: the game's walker clipping held clanrats by 2-15 m stays within 15 deg of its way (bearing 165-195 while pushing, melee flag lit); the twin's walker, slowed under 0.3 m/s in the clanrats' box, turned to them (53 deg with rect_gap) and ran cos(53 deg) of its speed to its point - the rect_gap stall. On with rect_gap: the walkpass2 push error 0.531 -> 0.346 m/s (centre line 0.335). Whole battles with rect_gap (exam replay): enemy routs 10.60 / 10.47 (off 9.70 / 10.68, game 16.0 / 16.3). Kept off with rect_gap.
contact.lone_rout_why: A lone man (a lord) and routers in melee, every rule in one block (tools/nn/sim/lone_rout.py; absent / empty: the old rules - lord_direction and pursuit_rate for a routing lone man too, no charge in a lone man's pursuit, a lone chaser striking across the pursuit's box gap). By the game's rules: the flank / rear penalty (defence x0.6 / x0.3, rounded half away from zero) is decided for every blow by where the striker stands against the struck man's facing (front within 45 deg, flank 45-135, rear beyond) and counts only when the striker faces his target; lone men take it as everyone (only the attribute flanking_immune turns it off - our lords have none); a router has no separate branch, but runs with his back to his chasers, does not turn to them and starts no attacks. A unit in pursuit of its routing attack target strikes with every blow of every man at its whole charge bonus x pursuit_charge_bonus_modifier (1.0), no decay over 13 s, no fatigue, in the hit chance and the damage; its interval as always (no extra blows), no damage multiplier on routers. direction 1.0: a routing lone target takes the flank / rear rule in full (from the rear: defence x0.3); a standing one keeps lord_direction 0 - the lord swarm probe's measure (infantry on his back or flank hurt him no more than on his front), kept where the rule and the measure disagree. share 1.0: a lone striker strikes a router at the rule in full, not at the formations' measured pursuit_rate 0.43 (kept for formations: pursuit_why). charge 1: a lone striker on his routing attack target - the whole charge bonus x the database's pursuit_charge_bonus_modifier, without the fatigue's multiplier (formations: none, the measure). own_reach 1: a lone chaser strikes a lone router only within his own reach (the regular contact, lord_reach_m + hold_m), not across pursue_gap_m (16 m between the boxes' edges: the routing mob strings out ~8 m beyond its box, a lone man does not); the router's melee flag still keeps the chase. By the rules: the Warlord on a routing General - defence 45 x 0.3 -> 14, 35 + 50 + 35 - 14 -> 90, p 0.89, a blow ~241 HP every 4 s -> ~54 HP/s; the General on a routing Warlord ~57. Checked in the game's records (build/diag_lordfix/blows.py, the 36 exam battles; a second: our General routing, the enemy General within 3 m with his target on him, no other enemy unit in melee within 20 m or targeting him within 30 m, no projectile at him): 0.22 blows a second (13 in 59 s, +-0.06), by the rules 0.89 / 4 = 0.22; the old rules 0.043; on our standing General in a duel 0.087 (29 in 356 s), by the rules 0.39 / 4 = 0.10. Within 4 m 0.16, within 6 m 0.10: blows within reach only. OPEN: one routing blow 261 HP (median 263, 13 blows) against 262 standing - the charge's ~+23 HP does not show in the blow's size (a blow's spread +-60 HP).
contact.hold_missile_why: hold_missile (melee.strikes): a missile unit under HOLD in melee (no attack order) strikes at hold_rate too, as a formation does; absent / false: in full (an older note said 0.99-1.01, its source not kept). The wavemiss probes (tools/nn/charge_probe.py plans wavemiss, wavemiss2; build/charge-probe/runs 20261009-072940, -073053 and the wavemiss2 pair; build/routmorale/wavemiss_report.py, wavemiss_twin.py): clanrats / swordsmen charging crossbowmen, archers, handgunners and Night Runners from 30 m; 10-90 s after contact the unordered shooters struck their attackers at 0.45 HP/s a man of theirs within 3.15 m of an enemy (4 lanes; the attackers lost 0.08 % of their health a second), the same shooters under an attack order 0.80 (8 lanes, 0.22 %/s) - 0.56 of it, as the melee probe's held formations (0.49-0.52); the twin without the rule: the attackers lost 0.27 %/s in both. The community knows the weak melee of unordered shooters as the 'weapon switching' loop (Steam Workshop 'Missile Troops - Melee Fix').
contact.missile_leave_why: missile_leave_any 1 (battle.py): a formation with a missile weapon under a MOVE leave_m or more away leaves melee whatever the direction of its point - through the enemy it touches too, and given before the contact too (leave_away_only stays for the formations without one: the P3 spearmen fought on). The 72 gate battles it1-it9 (11.10.2026): the game AI's shooters in melee under a run move (no target, point 10-1000 m) with the point through the nearest enemy (within 90 deg of the way to its centre) moved 0.92 of the seconds at 2.3 m/s median (1,456 s), away 0.96 at 3.0 m/s (1,229 s); given before the contact 0.91 at 2.8 m/s (625 s); the network's shooters told to move through the nearest enemy in melee 2.3 m/s at a run (937 s), 1.4 m/s at a walk (404 s). The replay before it: the AI's shooters in melee under a run move half of their steps not leaving (a move through, given before the contact: held fighting, 0.17 m/s). 0: leave_away_only for every formation.
contact.move_push_why: move_push on: a formation under a MOVE leave_m or more away that is not a leave (given before the contact, its point through the enemy: leave_away_only) is not held where it touches a standing enemy; it pushes on to its point, fighting (the melee flag; strikes as move_far_full), at a share of its order's speed (the walk / run tables) by the share of its front that the enemy formations it touches cover across its way (geometry.blocked_share, 0..1). The walkpass2 probe (tools/nn/charge_probe.py plan walkpass2, tools/nn/walkpass_probe.py; build/charge-probe/runs/20261013-033936 / -034309 at a run, -034116 / -034447 at a walk, 2 lanes a case): swordsmen (30 m front) told to move beyond held clanrats (30 m) with their straight way clipping them by 2 / 5 / 10 / 15 m (passed at 2.5-3.0 / 5.4-6.1 / 10.8-11.0 / 14.3-15.4 m: a share of the front 0.09 / 0.19 / 0.37 / 0.5) went on, the melee flag lit, at a net 2.68 / 2.39 / 0.78 / 0.26 m/s at a run and 1.33 / 0.97 / 0.73 / 0.31 at a walk from their first melee second until past the clanrats; straight through (the walkpass probe, -014012 / -014115) 0.26 / 0.12. The shares are these over the passport's run 3.0 / walk 1.5. None stepped aside more than 1.4 m (the controls at a 5 m gap the same): the game plans no way round an enemy, the unit pushes through it. The twin of the same 40 lanes, until past the clanrats: 2.44 / 1.47 / 0.92 / 0.53 m/s at a run, 1.23 / 0.91 / 0.79 / 0.38 at a walk (rule off: 0.93 / 0.65 / 0.32 / 0.08 and 0.69 / 0.58 / 0.13 / 0.12 - it stood where it touched). Left: at 10 m the game's walker, past the clanrats' centre, stays caught 5-15 m beyond it to the lane's end (the twin's goes free once the boxes part); at 2-5 m the game's walker keeps the melee flag at its point near the clanrats' rear 22-37 s (the twin 2 s); clanrats busy fighting spearmen beside the way shift towards them and are clipped by 0-6 m only. Exam v2 replay (build/compare/itS24 / itS24ai, 10 battles x 6 each; off -> on): enemy rout starts 10.21 -> 9.01 / 10.32 -> 10.05 a battle (game 16.0 / 16.3), enemy HP lost in melee 0.235 -> 0.223 / 0.226 -> 0.219 of its health per 100 s (game 0.249 / 0.270); walkers (the game's recorded far move) near a standing foe 319 -> 322 / 308 -> 317 s a battle, standing 0.56 -> 0.56 / 0.60 -> 0.59 (game 129 s, 0.19 / 92 s, 0.19). That table is no measure of this rule: 40-56 % of those replay seconds are ones where the game's unit routs or is shattered while the replayed one stands (the replay routs fewer units), and the rest are mostly units whose replayed course ran ahead of or behind the game's (training/simulator.md, What is missing).
contact.leave_away_why: leave_away_only 1: a MOVE order leave_m or more away is a leave (no strikes, not held) only when its point lies away from every enemy the unit touches (more than 90 deg off the way to that enemy's centre); a move point through the enemy (CA's planner gives far points 55-60 m on) keeps the unit fighting (contact.hold_move: at hold_rate). The probe build/probes7 P3 (clanrat spearmen attack Empire spearmen; the spearmen walk to a point 60 m ahead, through the attacker): the spearmen dealt 213 / 317 / 521 HP at 0-5 / 5-15 / 15-30 s after contact and 29 HP/s steady (answering with an attack order 361 / 319 / 377, 21 HP/s; held 221 / 161 / 166, 13 HP/s); the simulator's leaver 0 / 0 / 98. move_far_full 1 (a MOVE to a point leave_m or more away, given before the contact, strikes in full; a nearer one at hold_rate as R3's 5 m lanes): P3's push lane struck at 1.4x the attacking lane, hold_rate gave 0.5x, the rule 204 / 225 / 337 HP and 23 HP/s. Confirmed by the walkpass probe (tools/nn/charge_probe.py plan walkpass, 'through' lanes; build/charge-probe/runs/20261013-014012 at a run and -014115 at a walk; tools/nn/walkpass_probe.py): swordsmen told to move 40 m beyond held clanrats, straight through them, push in under the order (0.2 m/s, moving all the time) and strike 0.64 / 0.62 % of the clanrats' HP a second at 5-25 s after the contact - 0.56-0.69 of the same pair attacking (0.92 / 1.14 % a second in that probe's 'inmelee' lanes); the twin of those lanes 0.25 with 0 (hold_rate), 0.50 with 1. Exam v2 replay (20 battles x 6, build/lordrout): enemy rout starts 10.05 / 9.88 -> 10.63 / 10.83 a battle (game 17.3 / 17.1), enemy HP lost in melee 0.225 / 0.216 -> 0.228 / 0.225 of its health per 100 s (game 0.249 / 0.270). The game's rules (the melee rules check): a man starts a blow only when his body touches an enemy's (centres within r + r, 1.3 m for infantry, the enemy within 15 deg of his facing); own bodies do not let him through - a man of a second unit who runs into one of his own ahead stops and does not walk round; a unit gives targets to its front rank only; there is no 'go to another side' rule - a second unit comes at the same nearest side of the enemy as the first; no cap on the men striking one infantry man (only a soft spread when picking: +10 m for each man already striking him) and no multiplier for numbers (1.0). The game's mechanism is the engine's hit reaction (battle_entities hit_reactions_ignore_chance - the RPFM schema's name - 0 for all our infantry, 70-75 % for the lords; game_rules interrupt_mass_ratio_clamp_hit_reaction 0.4), with no number of the slowing in the database and none found online: the numbers are MEASURED. Not measured: throwing stars and pistols (musket by the database: included), cavalry and monsters (large: left out), lords (lone: left out, they ignore most hit reactions), routers (included: the same hit reaction). Replay of the 72 gate battles (5 copies, CPU): enemy lost at the end 0.496 -> 0.495 (game 0.571), ours 0.659 -> 0.655 (0.784), routs a unit 0.819 -> 0.822 (1.19), first contact 59.7 -> 60.8 s (61.2): within the noise.

Each man after every reload: his path from the muzzle to aim_frac (0.75) of the target man's height, blocked by a man of another own unit (a cylinder; a body holding the muzzle or within its radius of it blocks at any arc), costs him that shot; he takes the same target again, and the friends stand still, so the same men stay blocked every volley (the neighbour's men in files: a path in a file's band is blocked with the share of the rank spacing the window below the heads covers, between the files it passes them all). The unit's own men never block - every rank shoots - but for a unit in melee with its target. penetration.why: A projectile through several men (missile.py men_struck / penetration; line g43, 25.10.2026; 0: one man a hit). The game's rule (the database and its RPFM schema): projectiles.projectile_penetration names a row of projectile_penetration_junctions - max_penetration (a counter) and entity_size_cap; each man the projectile strikes adds his battle_entities projectile_penetration_resistance to the counter, and it goes on to the next man along its path only while the man is smaller than the cap and the counter is at most max_penetration (its speed x projectile_penetration_speed_change a man: 0.9, no effect on its damage). Our shooters: the Jezzails' and Long Rifles' medium_1 (max 1, cap medium) strike up to 2 infantrymen (resistance 1, size small), the Ironsides' low (max 2, cap small) and the pistols' low stop in the first (a small man is not below the cap), every other very_low (cap very_small) too; the Giant Rats (resistance 2) stop medium_1 in the first. In the rectangle simulator the factor on a pair's hits is 1 + P(a man k ranks behind the first) x (1 - shield)^k summed over the men past the first (the first man in the front rank by front_share, else evenly behind; the ranks along the line of fire from the bearing); a lone target takes 1 (the man behind him is another unit: not modelled). The fighters lab traces each projectile on to the next man past the one it struck (fighters/missile.py). max_men: the loop's cap (a no-limit projectile, max -1: none of ours). NOT MEASURED in the game: men killed per hit of the Jezzails / Long Rifles against a dense block (the probe 'дальний огонь').

The reaim rule alone was too weak: the twin fired whole volleys every 13 s to the end. NOT CHANGED: slings (only ~+1 s after the target's losses: open), direct fire and throwing weapons. OPEN: the mechanism of the threshold - presumably the men's own target men (a man whose man died aims again), which the unit-level threshold stands in for.
missile.reaim_why: reaim 1 (build/open_missile/spec.md S3; no new number): a man keeps his target man; when that man has died since his last shot he aims again for aim_s before his next one - the unit's volley waits aim_s x the share of its men whose target died since the last volley (state late: 1 - prod(1 - the target's men lost each step / its men)), so its men's interval is reload + aim_s x that share; a lone lord does not die man by man: the reload alone. The probe (build/missile, the game's recorded deaths, per-man model, reaim.txt): the volleys stay whole against a lone lord (0.8 of the men at once, the rest within 1.5 s) and turn into a stream against a formation from its first deaths; shots model / game at the end of the lanes without re-aim: arrows 1.18-1.39, slings 1.05-1.13, Night Runners 1.03-1.16; with it 1.10-1.26, 0.99-1.02, 0.96-1.05. OPEN: arrows still ~10 % high, pistols fire as a stream from the first volley (probe P2). retarget_from_none 1 (S4): taking a target from none is a new target (retarget_s without fire): the probe's archers / Night Runners drew the first projectile 1.5-2.5 s after a running target's centre came within range, not at once.
missile.replay_router_why: replay_router_release 1 (the replay of recordings only, tools/nn/sim/replay.py; no number): a shooter's recorded ATTACK on a unit that routs in the simulation while it stood in the recording at that second is released to fire at will (HOLD: the nearest standing enemy in range, else the nearest routing one). The game (build/midfight/router_fire.py, 170 network battles): after a shot target starts routing its shooter is on another target 1 s later in 42 % of 2430 cases, 3 s later in 60 %, still on it in 17-21 %; the game's AI fires at a router with a standing enemy in range in 11 % of its router-firing seconds (621 of 5799). The replay kept the recorded target, so where the simulation's rout came earlier its shooters went on shooting the router: the network's battles, 4 copies (build/midfight/diag.py): the game's AI's routers were shot 1.9-4.8x the game's seconds at 0-180 s after the first contact (sim 888 / 1603 / 1332 s, game 184 / 525 / 682), losing 54.9 / 82.2 / 58.1 thousand HP against 10.5 / 21.4 / 24.3. Where the recording's target was routing too (the controller chose a router) the order stays.

morale.lord_why: A lord's own morale. lord_own_aura false: the lord's aura (+4) reaches his army's other units, not himself. Measured (build/lordmorale/aura.py, all recorded runs): a lord at full health, calm, with a friend within 120 m stands at MoralePercent 1.129 (Empire General, 106 lord-battles: without his own aura (70 + 4 Hold the Line + 5) / 70 = 1.129, with it 1.186) and 1.083 (Skaven Warlord, 54: 65 / 60 = 1.083 against 1.150). single_combat 'losing': a single entity in melee always gets the database's losing_combat (-3), whatever the HP balance; missing: by the HP ratio like a formation. The game lords' morale in melee, regressed on the other terms (build/lordmorale/reg.py, combat.py), shows -3.8 points in melee (95 % CI -4.7 ... -3.0), flat in the HP balance (absolute or as shares); the ratio rule gave a lord +4 / +5 (winning) through most of his melee. The milder 'no winning bonus' (combat points capped at 0) gives 0 while even or winning: the measured -3.8 favours -3. With missile.single_entity_in_melee and fatigue.lord_why (batch 3), the replay of 22 gate battles x 6 copies (both sides on their recorded orders, build/batch3/lord_fate.py): our lord routed at least once 0.30 -> 0.44 (game 1.00), dead at the game's end 0.02 -> 0.06 (game 0.14), health left 0.35 -> 0.30 (game 0.11).
morale.windows_why: casualties_window sliding: recent casualties = HP lost in exactly the last casualties_s (4) s, extended casualties = in the last extended_s (60) s (the database's descriptions; its points: recent 6 / 10 / 15 / 33 / 50 % -> -6 ... -80, extended 10 / 15 / 33 / 50 / 80 % -> -4 ... -60); decay: decaying sums with those time constants. under_fire_s: 'under fire' (-5, ume_concerned_attacked_by_projectile) holds this long after the last projectile hit. Measured on the unit read-out probes of 27.09.2026 (build/unit-readout/runs, 1 s samples): the game's IsUnderMissileAttack is on through a barrage and goes off exactly 15 s after the last HP loss in 9 of 9 barrages, and morale starts to rise in that same second; PercentHpLostRecently after a volley holds one value 3 samples, then drops to 0 (a flat window of about 4 s, as the database says). Together (build/prespec/batch2.md section 2.3; the mechanics check's shooting targets, game 39 / 71 s waver / rout after the first shot for the archers' target, 154 / 177 for the slingers'): before (2 s, one decaying 30 s window) 35 / 68 and 154 / 184, 51 of 54; 15 s alone 25 / 68 (the archers' target wavers too early, 50 of 54); 15 s + decaying 4 s and 60 s 66 / 78 (50); 15 s + sliding 4 s and 60 s 46 / 68 and 165 / 184 (51); 15 s + sliding 4 s alone 68 / 90 (49). The single decaying 30 s window was fitted while 'under fire' lasted 2 s and stood in for it.
morale.expendable_why: expendable_scares_expendable: a routing expendable unit (attribute expendable: Skavenslaves) scares other expendable units within 100 m (-3 each, routing_friends) and no other unit; false: it scares nobody (the old rule). The database's attribute text: its rout scares only expendable units. Measured (build/prespec/batch2.md item 5, all fair recordings with morale): an expendable unit with one expendable friend newly routing within 100 m drops 3.0 points in 4 s (median, 350 cases); a normal unit at an expendable friend's rout 0.0 (178); the background 0.0.

strong_enemy.why: rule 'balance' (OFF for now: 'off' keeps the old rule below, strong_ratio; the effect at the end):the strong-enemy term is the database's scale - enemy_morale_penalty_value_min -3 at combat power enemy_morale_penalty_combat_power_min 4, linear to value_max -24 at combat_power_max 32, held beyond, 0 below 4 (_kv_morale_tables, no descriptions; linear between the pair like the database's other min/max pairs). Combat power = k x E / F (morale.strong_power): E = the standing enemies' strategic values (unit:strategic_value() = (combat potential + abilities' + missile x the ammunition curve) x health, the army collapse's 'cp' strength, matches the recordings) each x max(0, 1 - d / reach_m) (centre to centre); F = the unit's own + its standing friends' the same way. Sources: no formula in the community (searched 14.10.2026; fandom Leadership: 'if faster or stronger units are nearby'; the Empire morale guide on twcenter, search excerpt: 'the combat power and numbers of all units in a 75m radius are added to give friendly and enemy totals which are compared' - friends against enemies). k and reach_m are measured, not in the database: the morale probe strong2 (build/probes7/runs_morale, 2 battles; skavenslaves alone, a fearless enemy stops at about 100 / 80 / 60 / 40 m centre to centre; points from the level before it came): spearmen (strategic value 2.6x) 0 0 0 0, swordsmen (3.2x) 0 0 -3 -4, flagellants (5.0x) -3 -4 -5 -6, the General (7.6x, 95-35 m) -5 -7 -8 -9, swordsmen + spearmen side by side -4 -5 -6; least squares over these 19 points: k 1.975, reach_m 180 (largest error 0.43 point; k 2.0 already puts the spearmen at 40 m over the threshold); the probe T-F (65 / 45 / 30 m): swordsmen -3 -4 -4 (the rule -3.0 -3.6 -4.0), the General -7 -9 -9 (-7.2 -8.4 -9.4). Friends are counted because of the recordings (72 network-v-AI battles, build/latebattle/data; the scripts quiet.py / fit2.py / labels.py of agent-strongen): the same power without friends (E / own value) changes morale in 49 % of 20,140 quiet 10 s windows (full health, no melee or charge, flank flags and fatigue the same, an enemy within 140 m, no router within 110 m) by -3.7 points on average where the game's moved +0.08; with friends it changes none of them (the game: none); and the game's label 'enemies superior in strength and speed' rises with the points this rule gives: 0.4 % of unit-seconds at -3 ... -6, 1.9 % at -9 ... -12, 12 % at -18 ... -21, 40 % at -21 ... -24 (237 labelled unit-seconds, 97 % of them with a penalty by the rule). OPEN: greatswords (6.8x) gave nothing in strong2 at any distance (the rule -7.8 at 41 m) and archers next to the Warlord at 30 m nothing (the rule -3.2): what 'speed' in the label means is not found (no run-speed threshold fits both). Effect, old rule -> balance (the 72 network-v-AI battles x 4 copies, build/lordrout/replay72_mff1.json; the exam replays build/compare/itS24 / itS24ai x 6 copies, enemy routs a battle by build/lordrout/scripts_wt/rout_end.py): routs per unit 0.812 -> 0.782 (game 1.187), same winner 60 -> 55.5 of 72 (k 2.0: 0.779, 58), enemy routs a battle 9.70 -> 9.85 (network battles, game 16.0) and 10.68 -> 10.57 (AI battles, game 16.3). The old flat -3 was on in 51 % of the seconds before the game's routs (build/routgap/events_summary.json); the balance rule is on far less often (a unit in a line has friends near), so the rout deficit grows a little: the deficit is not in this term. Left OFF so the same-winner count does not drop; to switch on together with the fix of the rout deficit.

morale.strong_enemy_speed_why: strong_enemy.speed_ratio (morale.strong_power, rule 'balance' only; null: off): an enemy slower than speed_ratio x the unit's run speed (effects counted: Strength in Numbers x0.9) is not counted - the game's label is 'superior in strength and speed'. The probe strong2 (skavenslaves at 4.2 x 0.9 = 3.78 m/s): greatswords 2.8 m/s - nothing at 100-30 m, the only lane the balance rule missed; swordsmen 3.0, spearmen 3.0, flagellants 3.6, the General 3.4 - their points as before (any ratio 0.741-0.794 parts them the same way).
morale.strong_enemy_why: The old rule (morale.strong_enemy rule not 'balance'): a standing enemy within enemy_effect_range (70 m) worth strong_ratio times the unit or more (cost x health): the database's enemy_morale_penalty_value_min -3 (the game's label 'enemies superior in strength and speed'). The morale probe (T-F, build/morale, 06.10.2026: the tested unit stands, a fearless enemy stops at 65, 45 and 30 m): archers next to the Warlord (1.5x the worth, faster) or Night Runners (1.3x, faster) and spearmen next to clanrats (1.2x, faster) get nothing; skavenslaves next to swordsmen (3.0x, slower) -3 / -4, next to the General (4.8x, slower) -7 at 65 m and -9 at 45 / 30 m (it starts at ~120 m and grows as he comes). So speed is not needed and the ratio's threshold lies between 1.5 and 3.0: strong_ratio 3 (the smallest measured ratio that showed it). OPEN: the scale to -24 by 'combat power' 4-32 (the General's -9; no formula found, searched 06.10.2026) and the reach beyond 70 m; the recordings show the label at a median 1.9x (several enemies summed, build/morale_spec 2.10). REMOVED: strong_enemy_points -3 for any enemy worth more: it stood in for the +5 flanks secure the old rule gave in melee.

The community (Steam WH3 discussion 'Broken units & balance of power + army losses'): broken units count as active with whatever CP remains, only shattered ones drop out. Step replay (H 10, 2 copies; 72 gate / 20 exam), routs from MoralePercent 0.5-0.75 sim/game: free 2.82 / 1.98 -> 2.26 / 1.76, on the game's places and losses 2.04 / 1.30 -> 1.53 / 1.07; all routs free 1.00 / 1.11 -> 0.92 / 1.07. 72 whole battles (4 copies): same winner 60.5 -> 59, routs a unit 0.779 -> 0.789 (game 1.187), own_won 0.253 -> 0.240 (game 0.125). Ability cp does not run out (CA forum 6037: missile value falls with ammo, spells and abilities do not). The database's thresholds (enemy >= 2.6 x own, own <= 0.22 x own start; a mod author's thread 5270 names the same pair) on this strength: met at the onset second of the game's army destruction in 0.94 of 84 onsets (recorded value 0.93; the old fit 0.89), within 1 s 0.90 (old 0.69), within 5 s 0.96 (old 0.85), no false triggers. Removed: lord_value_scale 1.65, ammo_empty 0.32 / ammo_empty_direct 0.57 (fits of the old cost-based value). In the open-loop replay army destruction fires by the end in 0.15 of the ownloss battles against the game's 0.96 with either strength: the replay's losing army still holds 0.23 of its strength at the game's onset (the game 0.15) - it loses health too slowly in the last two minutes (a damage gap, OPEN), not the rule. Before: CCO morale fields in 69 of 175 completed fair battles (build/collapse): 65 sides show Army losses. BalanceOfPowerPercent is reconstructed by strategic_value with routers weighted 0.5 (mean absolute bar error 0.00041 versus 0.0121 at full weight); shattered units contribute zero. The database's 2.6 enemy/own and 0.22 own/start thresholds on that strength time 64/65 onsets within 5 s (median 0 s, mean absolute error 0.57 s). Three additional triggers occur only in final frames after the last standing unit routes, not before defeat. Value follows HP, not men. Starting lord values are 950/900 versus multiplayer cost 600/525: approximate with lord_value_scale 1.65. Missile value is HP times a normalised sigmoid of whole-unit ammunition remaining: slope 14, midpoint 0.25, empty fractions 0.309/0.312/0.323 for archers/slingers/night runners and 0.570 for direct-fire Free Company. Generic floors 0.32/0.57 plus the lord scale approximate the recorded pools (bar error 0.0051, 58/65 onsets within 5 s, no missed onsets, median 0 s); other missile types are not fitted. Army losses propagate globally: 271/275 units standing just before onset show the effect, median delay 0 s; median routing friends within 100 m is 0. All 274 army-loss shatters before a third rout cross the database's broken lower edge (-50 points). Routers keep losing morale under army destruction even away from enemies and cannot rally out of it. No lord-fall points tie in (a routed lord costs his aura only, lord_fall.why): 33/65 onsets have a standing lord; 42/65 have no friend newly routing in the previous 3 s. Full-strength routers were rejected: three-gate replay trade -0.090/-0.081/-0.244 versus baseline -0.090/-0.080/-0.252; the apparent 59/65 onset match mainly followed shattering instead of predicting it. Shattering below -50 is limited to army destruction. At game end, scoped replay trade is -0.094/-0.088/-0.246 versus baseline -0.090/-0.080/-0.252 (game -0.306/-0.260/-0.407): mean absolute trade error 0.18356 to 0.18137, but the third gate regresses, so the all-three acceptance criterion is unmet. In the first copies only 3/22 own armies reach the measured conditions by game end; prior combat divergence remains.

morale.combat_why: Winning / losing the fight (+3 / +6 / +8, -3 / -8, the database): by (HP dealt + 1) / (HP taken + 1) over the melee AND the missile balance between enemies (dealt / taken and shot_dealt / shot_taken, decaying with recent_s), while the unit is in melee, shooting (its fire flag) or shot at by an enemy shooting at it now. The morale probe (T-D): archers shooting clanrats / skavenslaves with no answer show 'Одерживают верх' +8 from their first kill to 1.5-2 s after they stop shooting (10 s between volleys without a gap); spearmen shot by slingers show 'Несут потери' (-8) until the slingers stop. The community rule (Goumin's guide): a unit is losing if engaged with an enemy taking less damage than it; thresholds unknown. combat_lost 0.1: losing shows only once the unit has lost this share of its health, winning only once an enemy it fights (in contact, or the target it shoots / is shot by) has - measured in the probe, 6 lanes: the term appears 0.5-1 s after the loser crosses 10 % lost and never before (archers' targets at 7.5 s and 17.5 s, the shot spearmen at 20 s after the first volley's 6 %, spearmen in front fights at 30 / 35 / 49 s); it equals the first step of the database's casualty table (total_casualties_penalty_10), which the game may use - OPEN. combat_ratio thresholds stay FITTED (1.5 / 2.5 / 4). combat_ratio losing / losing_significantly: the losing side has its own thresholds (HP taken / dealt) - losing (-3) once a unit takes more than it deals x losing (1.0: Goumin's WH3 kv_rules guide, 'a unit is losing if engaged with an enemy taking less damage than it' - no even band), losing significantly (-8) from x losing_significantly (2.5: the morale probe T-D's front fights, spearmen against clanrats - an HP balance of 0.32 showed -8 in the game, 0.58-0.63 showed -3; the old rule gave -3 to 0.32). Winning keeps slightly / yes / significantly (FITTED 1.5 / 2.5 / 4; winning from 1 changed nothing in the replay). Checked (build/routmorale, 09.10.2026): the melee pairs - pair_spear_v_slave fight 173 -> 174 s (game 232; the earlier note's 179 s was with other rules), pair_spear_v_clanrat our spearmen waver 277 -> 256 s (game 251), rows within 20 % 19 -> 20 of 36; the replay of the 72 gate battles (4 copies) routs a unit 0.762 -> 0.788 (game 1.19), rallies 0.39 -> 0.41 (0.60), our units routed 0.636 -> 0.632 (0.937), skill -1 -> 0 %.

secure.why: Flanks secure (+5, the database's ume_encouraged_flanks_secure): no standing enemy within enemy_m (centre to centre), or friends that are not lords within side_m at BOTH sides (side_deg off the unit's facing, left and right); never while a flank is threatened (lf / rf / bf). The community rule (Goumin's WH3 morale guide, steamcommunity 2776861563): 'friendly units entirely surrounding: +5'. The morale probe (build/morale, 06.10.2026; src/entries/morale_probe.lua): spearmen standing, an enemy closing by steps - +5 at 150-310 m, gone between 148.2 and 144.4 m in both lanes (0.5 s samples: 146 m), the same with one friend 32 m at the side, one 30 m in front or the lord 30 m at the side (none of them secures); in melee with two friends 34 m at both sides +5 holds (65 against 60 points without them, 2 battles). side_m 40 and side_deg 30-150: the recordings (build/morale_spec probe2-5: friends beside within 40 m, not in front or behind); the database's neighbour_effect_range and open_flanks_effect_range (120 m) do not match the 146 m centre to centre (edge to edge 132 m in the probe) - their geometry is not known. Before: +5 with any standing friend (lords too) within 120 m: nearly always, in melee too (agreement with the recorded labels 73 %, this rule 87 %).

moving.why: The charge's morale goes with the unit charging, i.e. moving under an attack order (u mv, its own move last step, > 0.3 m/s): a block (block_s 6 = the database's charge_timeout 60 in tenths of a second, the unit of waver_base_timeout and broken_finish_base_timeout) is followed by another while the unit still moves under the attack order, with no cap (blocks ignored); melee_start: a unit in melee that moves under an attack order with no block running starts one. Measured on the recordings (92 battles of the step replay, the label 'Натиск' = MoraleGreatestEffect): at a block's end another block followed in 54-64 % of the cases with the game's moving flag on and 0-2 % with it off, for the 1st, 2nd and 3rd block alike (6,474 / 2,676 / 1,161 blocks; the label lasts 6 / 12 / 18 / 24 s in 3,808 / 1,932 / 499 / 155 episodes - the old cap of 2 blocks cut the last two); deep in melee (20 s+ of contact) 93 % of the label's starts came with the moving flag on against 12 % of such seconds, never without a move; after a unit there starts to move its morale rose +5.4 points in 6 s under an attack order (-1.1 under a move order, -1.2 not moving). The probe T-B (4 lanes, 6 + 6 s) is the approach case of the same rule.

charge.why: The charge's morale (+15, the database's charge_bonus): blocks of block_s from the start of the charge sprint (battle.py: an attack order, the target's edge within the unit's charge distance, not yet in melee: the same sprint that gives the charge), a next block when one ends while the unit still sprints or its charge has landed (u charge > 0), at most `blocks` a charge; none while routing. Measured: the recordings' label 'Натиск' lasts exactly 6 s (1,686 episodes) or 12 s (1,006), build/morale_spec probe.json; the morale probe (T-B, 4 lanes: attack at a run from 150 and 40 m, at a walk from 80 m, a walk to 10 m then an attack): the label starts at a gap of 24.6-27.5 m edge to edge (4.5-6.5 s before contact; centre to centre 36-40 m), lasts 6 + 6 s in every lane (to 6-7.5 s after contact), points +15 through the 15 % smoothing. The database's charge_timeout 60 is not a cooldown (a unit charges again within 19 s, median of the recordings); its meaning is not known. OPEN: the start at the sprint's 30 m (charge_distance_commence_run) is 0.6-1.4 s before the game's (charge_distance_adopt_charge_pose, 25 m, may be the trigger: not in the passport yet).

Rallies / re-routs / routs per AI unit: game 0.42 / 0.24 / 0.61, fixed 0.46 / 0.35 / 0.74, target 0.27 / 0.16 / 0.55, min -0.17 0.35 / 0.24 / 0.63 (gaps 0.10 / 0.25, the cap: within 0.01); our units' routs game 1.57, fixed 1.09, target 0.93. Mechanics 51 / 54 with each. Gap card of gate 20261005-161910 (8 copies, items 1-4 of batch 3 on): routs per unit own / enemy game 1.52 / 0.58, fixed 1.04 / 1.08, target 0.85 / 0.84; trade game -0.385, fixed +0.037, target +0.022 (min -0.17: 1.02 / 0.92, +0.009). The whole check (tools.nn.sim.check): routs / rallies a battle game 22.5 / 13.0, fixed 18.1 / 10.9, target 13.0 / 5.9; same winner game-AI 22 / 26 -> 21, network 122 / 163 -> 123. Left OFF: no variant meets both the counts and the timing (the game also rallies units with nothing left, and they rout again gradually, not at 10 s; that rule is not found).

attacked_first.why: Attacked in the flank / rear (-6 / -14) by the side each attacker's contact BEGAN on, held while that pair stays in contact (state.PAIRS hit_sec; battle.py), instead of the side it strikes from this step. The database's own text of was_attacked_in_flank / _rear is 'first contact from the flank / rear'; the morale probe T-A: the label from the rear attacker's first blow to its leaving (29 s). The recordings (92 battles, the recorded target field as the attacker, centre angles): the game shows 'Атакованы с тыла' in 18 % of the melee seconds where the contact began in the rear and the attacker is now in front (the struck unit turned to it), 22 % where it began and stays in the rear, 8.5 % where it began in front and is now in the rear; one attacker: 'с фланга' 10 % at a first-contact angle of 75-90 deg against 4 % at 0-15 deg. The label is only the greatest effect, so the shares are lower bounds.

combat_shooter.why: Winning / losing for a unit out of melee that shoots: only the HP it exchanges with the enemy it aims at (its missile HP dealt against that enemy's missile HP dealt, when that enemy aims back at it), not the fire of other enemies on it (battle.py ctx fight_dealt / fight_taken; morale.terms). The recordings (92 battles, settled 10 s windows of shooters in a fight whose foe has lost 10 %): the game's morale needs +8 for the fight term at every balance of all HP from 0.67 up and +5 below 0.4 (355 windows), where the balance of all HP gave -3 / -8; 'Одерживают верх' needs +8.9 (median, 3,202 windows of idle shooters) and the old rule gave 0 in 47 % of them. lord_fall.why: A lord's fall: his aura goes (battle.py: the aura counts standing lords only) and, on top, his army's other units get points by HOW he fell. KILLED (health 0): the database's ume_concerned_general_died_recently -16 for recent_s, then ume_concerned_general_dead -10 to the end (killed: true). Routed OFF THE MAP (gone with men left): ume_concerned_general_fled_recently -16 for fled_s, then nothing (fled: true). ROUTED or shattered, still on the field: `routed` points (0: the aura alone). rout_death_s: a faction whose routed lord crumbles to death counts him killed that long into his rout. Measured 05.10.2026 (tools/nn/lord_fall.py, 15 in-game battles, build/lord-fall/analysis.json; build/lorddeath/timeline.py): the lord killed at a fixed moment, 20 s into melee (Empire, Skaven, Vampire Counts, 2 battles each): the two idle units out of his aura and 115+ m from any enemy (12 unit-deaths) show 'general died recently' and drop -3 / -7 / -13.5 / -16 points 1 / 2 / 5 / 10 s after, hold -16, the effect turns into 'general dead' at 45.5-46 s and the units stand at -10 from ~50 s to the recording's end (60 s); identical in all three factions. The ramp is the morale update itself (max(1, 15 % of the gap) a 0.5 s tick: a step of -16 gives -4.4 / -7.6 / -12.9 / -15.4), so the points are a step. The two fighting units within his aura: -6 / -10 / -17.5 / -21...-25 at 1 / 2 / 5 / 10 s (aura and melee on top). The lord routed by script (morale_behavior_rout; Empire, Skaven, 2 battles each): the idle units 0 at every moment, the fighting ones about the aura (-0.5...-6.8 at 10 s net of the control); general_fled_recently does not show while the lord is on the field. Leaving the map (build/prespec/specs.md section 1, recorded battles with morale texts from 02.10.2026): a shattered lord who routs off the map edge (4 cases, 10-17 % health) gives his army 'general fled recently': the standing units -14...-17 points within 10 s (3 battles, 18 units), the effect lasts ~120 s (747 -> 867 s, 782 -> 901 s; the other two recordings ended sooner) and no 'general dead' follows: fled_s 120 (2 timed cases, medium confidence). A lord killed while routing (4 cases) gives the same 'died recently' -> 'dead' after 45 s. Vampire Counts' routed lord shatters and crumbles (health -12 % a second), dies at 8-8.5 s, and his army gets 'general died recently' from 8.5 s, 'general dead' from 53.5 s: rout_death_s 8 (the simulator has no Vampire Counts units: config only). The same battles in the simulator (build/lorddeath/sim_fall.py: the recorded places, Empire and Skaven, the fight pairs attacking, the enemy held fearless): idle units -4.4 / -7.6 / -14 / -16 / -16 / -16 / -10 at 1 / 2 / 5 / 10 / 20 / 40 / 60 s after the death (game -3 / -7 / -13.5 / -16 / -16 / -16 / -10; 0 throughout before this rule), fighting units net of the control -5.5 / -9.6 / -16 / -20 / -20 / -20 / -14 (game, Empire and Skaven -6.4 / -9.3 / -16.5 / -16 / -16.9 / -19.1 / -13.5; before -2 / -4 / -4 / -4 / -4 / -4 / -4); the rout: idle 0, fighting -2 / -4 / -7 / -7 / -4 / -4 / -4 (game -2.6 / -3.6 / -7 / -3.3 / -0.3 / -2.6 / -0.5), unchanged. Natural falls (02.10.2026, build/simacc/lordfall2.py): in all 75 recorded lord falls of the fair battles the lord shattered with 2-50 % of his health left (none was killed), and the standing units of his army (167 unit-falls, 35 falls) changed by 0 points in the 10 s before, -1 at the fall, -3.2 / -4.3 / -4.7 / -4.8 (mean; median -3) 2 / 4 / 6 / 10 s after, -7 at 20 s - about the aura; the database's -16 / -10 on every fall gave -9 / -14 / -17 / -18 and routed 39 % of the army within 10 s (the game 21 %). So from task 20 to 05.10.2026 every fall was 0 / 0 (right for routs, wrong for deaths). The armies' collapse at the end of the game's battles is a rule not tied to the lord (collapse.why).

A unit starts to waver only below the shaken band's lower edge (ums_shaken_threshold_lower 12 points) and stays wavering while its points are at the wavering band's upper edge (ums_wavering_threshold_upper 16) or below; it is shaken below the steady band's lower edge (ums_steady_threshold_lower 30) and steady again only above the shaken band's upper edge (ums_shaken_threshold_upper 32). Measured: the recordings (92 battles of the step replay, 1 s, points = MoralePercent x the card's leadership): of 33,791 seconds at 12-16 points 5.3 % wavered when the unit came from above 16 and 98.2 % when it came from below 12; wavering starts at 9.9-11 points (p25-p75), 3.2 % at 12 or more; the morale probe's lanes (0.25-0.5 s): all 32 starts 12 -> 11 points, all 9 ends 16 -> 17, shaken -> steady at 33. The step replay of 92 battles (build/morale-hyp/sr_*, sim / game; waver_band, the floor, shatter_by men, routing_net and rally_weak on together against all off): rout starts 0.98 -> 0.95, rallies 1.02 -> 1.05, shatters 4.09 -> 0.64, waver starts 1.66 -> 1.02, wavering seconds 1.06 -> 0.86; alone (the 46 smaller battles): waver starts 1.50 -> 0.98, wavering seconds 1.01 -> 0.83 (the simulator's points sit above the game's at shaken and wavering, +0.03-0.04 MoralePercent a window), routs 0.932 -> 0.924.

Proved in the game by the probe timer (tools/nn/morale_probe.py, build/morale-probe/timer.json, 4 battles x 6 lanes, normal difficulty; the key changed in the probe's own pack, tools/build.py --kv): with the game's 25, units whose morale fell through wavering in ~1 s (the engine killing half their men a second) routed 3.0 s after the first wavering sample, 2.1 s of it below 0; with 250 three lanes routed 25.5 / 25.5 / 25.5 s after the wavering, sitting up to 24 s below 0 (MoralePercent -0.03...-0.17) without a rout; with 0, 1.2 s (as soon as below 0). Units that wavered longer than the timer routed 0.3-0.6 s after reaching 0 in all three variants, and units whose attackers left at the wavering recovered in all three (no 'casualties while wavering -> rout at the timer's end'). So 25 is tenths of a second and the timer is the least wavering before a rout, not a delay after 0. The recordings agree (20 gate sets, 2509 first routs, 1 Hz): no rout before 3 recorded seconds of wavering; the 'MoralePercent <= 0 without a rout' of build/simreal/morale_timers.md is exactly 0 (1574 samples at 0, 663 below 0): the game's points are whole numbers (MoralePercent in steps of 1 / leadership). stealth.why: Hiding and spotting (tools/nn/sim/stealth.py; line g43, 25.10.2026; on 0: nobody hides, every unit is seen - the simulator before g43; old armies have no unit that hides, so their battles do not change). The game's rules (the database and the community's breakdown of the engine): hiding is a flag of the whole unit; it hides once more than share_hide of its men stand on ground that hides them and stays hidden while more than share_keep - for the attribute stalk any ground (our maps have no woods: only stalk units hide - the Gutter Runners, the Huntsmen); it becomes hidden to the enemy hide_s after it began to meet that, unseen; out of cover while hidden and unseen it stays hidden grace_s more; an enemy sees it within its spotting distance (land_units spot_dist_scrub: 80 m, the Jezzails 160 m; + fresh_bonus_m for the first fresh_s after it hid) x its hiding_scalar (0.8 the Gutter Runners), edge to edge (the Gutter Runners within 64 m, 80 m just after hiding; by the Jezzails within 128 m); firing reveals it (its shooting state: a target taken and the aim done - the attribute snipe would not, none of our hiding units has it), so does melee; an attack order does not (reveal.attack_order 0: the probe of 25.10.2026 - Gutter Runners ordered to attack a target beyond their range stayed hidden) and running does not (the probe: they ran hidden from 150 to 63 m). Hidden: the enemy's shooters do not take it, an attack order on it is none (HOLD), the enemy's blows do not fall on it, the enemy's morale and skirmish runs do not count it, the network's side sees its last place only (vis). start_hidden 1: an ASSUMPTION - a unit that can hide is hidden from the battle's first second (the deployment). The probe 'скрытность' (25.10.2026, 3 battles; a CHECK, nothing fitted): Gutter Runners seen by swordsmen (spotting 80) at 66.6 / 64.8 / 62.9 m standing / walking / running (the rule 64), Huntsmen by the Jezzails (160) at 163.5 m (the rule 160), measured between the nearest men; firing reveals 0.6 s after it begins (before the first projectile); hidden again 5.0 s after the fire stops; a unit without stalk is always seen (checked to 484 m).

skirmish.why: The game's skirmish mode (tools/nn/sim/skirmish.py): a shooter with the mode on (the game's toggle; the database's can_skirmish) runs away, over its order, from an enemy that comes at it, and shoots again when none does. on: the rule; network 0: the toggle `sk` is on only where the game's AI rule plays (scenario.build: the side's `ai` unless it says 'skirmish'; abilities.set_rule: the scripts' sides on, a network's off) - as in the game, where the game's AI keeps the mode on for its shooters (all 8 battles of 10.10.2026, build/skirm/f_farpoint.py: the far point of its run only with sk on) and the bridge switches it off for the network's (--skirmish off; the gate sets it1-it9: our shooters never ran so); network 1 gives the mode to every unit that can skirmish (a later option for the network). Sources: the probes 'skirmish' (build/charge-probe/runs/20261010-033006, -033102: a halted shooter charged by melee infantry from 60 m, mode on / off, five shooters, 2 lanes each; build/skirm/b_lanes.py) and 'skirmish2' (-053344, -053448: slave slingers, archers, crossbowmen with the mode on; infantry running PAST 30 m beside the shooter (edge ~9 m), attacking its NEIGHBOUR 30 m beside it, attacking it (control), 2 lanes each; build/skirm/j_skirm2.py, build/skirmsim/angle2.py). Who counts (cone_deg 40, moving_mps 0.3): a standing enemy that moves (over the observed moving flag's 0.3 m/s) with its way within 40 deg of the line from its centre to the shooter's. The infantry running past started the same run at the same distance (Empire 40-42 m, slingers 31-32 m nearest man to nearest man) - not an attack order but the way it moves; the run ended after 5-7.5 s (10-24 m) though the infantry went on past 14-19 m away: when its way turned 28-53 deg off the line to the shooter (median 40 deg; pass and neighbour lanes, 10 run ends; its way at the run starts 21-47 deg, median 28), the attacker of the shooter came at 2-12 deg and the run never ended; the neighbour's attacker made the Empire shooters run 2-10 s, the slingers (their gap reached later, the way already 35-40 deg off) 0-0.5 s. start_gap_m: nearest man to nearest man (soldier_gap: the rectangles of the men's places, (files - 1) h x (ranks - 1) v) at the fire stop, the simulator's measure on the recorded places, bearings and men of both probes (build/skirmsim/conv2.py): Empire 43.9 m (median of 18 lanes, 38.8-48.5; the game's own soldier gap 38.5-41.7), Skaven 33.1 m (median of 10, 30.4-37.1 bar one 49.5; game 31.2-35.5); the default is the Empire's (the militia not measured). The formations' edge gap (geometry.pairwise) is not it: a narrow deep column passing aside reached it 8-10 m later along its way, its way already 33-35 deg off, and the twin's runs past lasted 2 s against 6-9. stop_gap_m 82: the same measure where the 'skirmish' runs that got away stopped, 73-95 m (6 lanes: Empire 80-95, Night Runners 73-77). The run is at the passport's run speed with the turn on the move (turn.move_turn: the fire stops ~0.5-1.5 s before the move, as the game's). melee_run 1: caught, the shooter runs on (the game: 73 % of a caught skirmisher's melee seconds moving away, striking half as hard) - a leave (battle.py: it strikes nobody, the attackers in contact strike it; contact.pin_s 0: not held in place); a run starts only out of melee; 0: a caught shooter stands and fights. Who keeps it (v3; build/skirm/k_run_ends.py, n_backoff_ends.py, o_merged.py, p_still.py on the 72 replay battles: the game AI's runs = its far ordered point, merged over breaks <= 2 s, median 7 s, 3-16): a coming enemy with its attack order on the shooter keeps the run to stop_gap_m (the game's runs so chased ended 0.057 a second, 0.09-0.15 at 70-100 m - the probe's stop at ~85 m; attacker_end_per_s 0, the 0.057 tried: the replay as without it); a coming enemy that attacks another (or no one) ends it with other_end_per_s 0.18 a second at any distance (338 ends in 1554 s; the probe's 'pass' runs 5-7.5 s), a fixed hash draw per battle id, unit and step (morale's rally_hazard's); such an enemy starts a run only as it comes within start_gap_m from beyond it (sk_in: any standing enemy not attacking the shooter within the gap, whatever its way) - not again while it stays inside (else the hazard ended nothing: 0.86 runs a minute, game 0.45). With v2's keep (any coming enemy within the stop gap) the game's run would have gone on in 72 % of the seconds it ended. show_far_point 1: the run's far point is the unit's observed ox, oz while it runs, as the game shows it (the order's own point kept in sk_ox, sk_oz); the replay measures the run's state by it, the same as the game's. Without the body Warp Lightning kills about half the game's men on the probe's casts (its 224 AP bolts kill every man touched; the per-man replay 0.52), with it 0.87.
